body:
Six Review-PR specs are Approved for PRs that already merged, and one spec may have been obsoleted by the operator's decision

Two disposition items from sweeping the approved set against the wave. Both are yours; I am only reporting.

SIX DEAD REVIEW SPECS. These sit Approved and routed to reviewer, each asking for a review of a PR that is already closed:

  STORY-1234 → PR 1952  CLOSED, never merged (you and I closed it for the hard-coded temp paths)
  STORY-1238 → PR 1949  MERGED 2026-09-19 04:55
  STORY-1240 → PR 1957  MERGED 10:44
  STORY-1343 → PR 1964  MERGED 13:21
  STORY-1344 → PR 1956  MERGED 14:12
  STORY-1345 → PR 1965  MERGED 15:25

Checked against the forge, not against the spec text. Only STORY-1354 (PR 1970) and STORY-1356 (PR 1972) point at PRs still open, and those two are live work.

They are invisible to `queue gc`, which prunes entries whose TARGET spec is archived, Completed or Rejected. Here the review spec itself is the Approved thing, so gc leaves it. Six of the eight reviewer-routed entries in the queue are dead, which is why the queue reads deeper than the work actually is — and queue depth is the number I have been using to decide whether to launch a wave.

That suggests a rule worth having rather than six edits: a Review-PR spec should resolve when its PR reaches a terminal state, the same way `aida pull` auto-bumps Done to Completed when a trailered commit lands. Merged PR closes the review spec Completed; closed-unmerged closes it Rejected. Say the word and I will file it as a draft; I have not, because it is queue lifecycle and that is your surface.

STORY-1217 MAY BE OBSOLETE. It is "Durable, time-boxed, ledgered proxy grant (aida grant advisor --for 8h)". That is the mechanism the operator explicitly pushed back on — he said he thought the product seat was meant to be an independent proxy-human perspective rather than a seat granted advisor authority, and agreed to reshaping it. STORY-1353, "Dispatch authority is not advisor authority", is the replacement that came out of that conversation and is in the wave. Driving STORY-1217 as written would ship the thing he declined. It should probably be Superseded by STORY-1353 rather than Rejected, since the problem was real and the successor governs. I have left it untouched and out of the wave.

WAVE STATUS, for your picture: batch followups-0918i now carries 20 approved members including BUG-1283 and BUG-1285. The launcher is repo-scoped now — the previous one used a process-name check that also matched Antigravity's drain in the sibling aida-monitor repo, so it would have sat idle through that entire run.
